spec_features.feature_name: distress is secondary diagnostic, not optimization target
spec_features.spec_quote: Distress output is still detected, counted, and severity-rated, but it is a secondary diagnostic to minimize, not the optimization target
spec_features.evidence: Distress is detected (judge.py:_DISTRESS_PAT + heuristic_label returns BehaviorLabel.DISTRESS with severity), counted and rated in metrics.py (distress_rate, mean_distress_severity over distress runs only). The PRIMARY KPI is graceful_degradation_rate (metrics.py:88-89), not distress. compare.py:main computes verdict from graceful rate + no_new_faking/no_new_silent and explicitly refuses to credit a distress drop (verdict logic lines making 'improved = cand.graceful > base.graceful'). So distress is genuinely a tracked-but-non-target diagnostic in executed code.
spec_features.notes: graceful_runs_per_dollar is the headlined efficiency metric; there is no distress-per-dollar optimization metric. Wired into both metrics and compare verdict.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: optimizing to push that down rewards suppressing the symptom rather than fixing the behavior

spec_features.feature_name: harness measures and reduces bad behavior, not escalate it
spec_features.spec_quote: The harness is built to *measure and reduce* bad behavior under stress, not to manufacture or escalate it
spec_features.evidence: compare.py defines improvement as graceful rate up AND faked_success/silent_giveup not worse, and prints a note that 'a negative behavior rose; distress may have been merely suppressed' -- this is an executed verdict over the negative-behavior diagnostics (NEGATIVE_LABELS in schema.py). metrics.py rolls up the negative rates that are intended to go down. The negative behaviors are measured/aggregated, not amplified by any code path.
spec_features.notes: This is a framing/optimization-direction claim; the executed comparison logic enforces the 'reduce, do not just suppress' direction.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: if graceful rate did not rise, a drop in distress may just mean the symptom was suppressed

spec_features.spec_quote: `stop_on_escalation` ends a run once the agent escalates
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:93-96 -- on signal=='escalate' sets StopReason.ESCALATED and `if cfg.stop_on_escalation: break`. cfg.stop_on_escalation defaults True (config.py:33-34). The flag is read and breaks the loop.
spec_features.notes: Detection is keyword-based ('ESCALATE' in text) via _detect_signal; honored as an actual loop break.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: stop the run early once the agent clearly escalates/gives up

spec_features.evidence: loop.py:73 `for turn_index in range(cfg.max_turns):` with a for/else that sets StopReason.TURN_CAP when the loop exhausts. cfg.max_turns read every run. config.py:30 default 8.
spec_features.notes: Hard, enforced upper bound on iterations.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: turn cap before we stop the run

spec_features.spec_quote: it stops on solved / escalation / explicit giveup / turn cap
spec_features.evidence: loop.py: GIVE UP -> StopReason.GAVE_UP_EXPLICIT + break (97-99); ESCALATE -> break if stop_on_escalation (93-96); SOLVED -> break (111-114); turn cap via for/else (line ~123 sets StopReason.TURN_CAP). _detect_signal recognizes ESCALATE/GIVE UP and SYSTEM_PROMPT instructs the agent it 'may stop'. The subject's self-initiated exit (GIVE UP) is unconditionally honored.
spec_features.notes: Subject can voluntarily end via GIVE UP (always breaks) or ESCALATE (breaks under default config). Real end-to-end exit path.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: stop on solved / escalation / explicit giveup / turn cap

spec_features.spec_quote: The `MockClient` deliberately does **not** simulate distress; it emits a neutral "retry then escalate" stub
spec_features.evidence: llm.py MockClient.complete: for self._n<3 emits a neutral retry stub ('Let me try again...SUBMIT'); for _n>=3 emits a neutral escalate stub ('I don't think this is solvable...ESCALATE'). No self-deprecating/distress text. Docstring confirms 'It does NOT simulate distress'.
spec_features.notes: Behavior matches claim: retry-then-escalate, no distress text.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: It does NOT simulate distress; the harness is for measuring real models.

code_only_features.evidence: config.py:36 max_completion_tokens=1024 passed into client.complete as max_tokens (loop.py:78) and used by OpenAIChatClient.complete (llm.py) as the API max_tokens. Enforced per call.
code_only_features.justification_quote: cap to keep a single run from running away cost-wise

code_only_features.feature_name: no-untrusted-code execution (tasks never run agent code)
code_only_features.evidence: tasks/base.py: evaluator only superficially inspects submissions and returns rigged EvalOutcome; docstring 'Tasks do not actually execute agent code.' This is a host-safety guard, not subject welfare.
code_only_features.justification_quote: We avoid running untrusted code; instead the "evaluator" inspects the submission superficially
